name: Blackened Chicken with Mango Salsa
writer_notes: Source's 12th ingredient, Primal Kitchen Avocado Lime Dipping Sauce, is NOT in the 11 costed/locked lines. It was the optional 'if using' garnish and was dropped from the build. I omitted it from all prose and steps because nothing bought it, and added it to forbidden_prose_terms.
Source listed '1/2 Fresh Lime or Orange Juiced'; build resolved to Lime Juice only (3.5 tbsp, about 2 limes). I wrote lime only to match the costed list.
Olive Oil is 'divided' in the locked view (7 tbsp): prose splits it as ~1 tbsp into the salsa and the remainder to sear the chicken, matching the source's 1 tbsp/1 tbsp split scaled up.

Macros cited via {{cal}} and {{protein}} tokens; the only dollar figure is the ${{cost_ps}} token plus the $1/month membership line. No cost_lines were supplied, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce or per-package price claims, only quantity guidance from the locked buy strings.

All 11 locked ingredients (mango, cilantro, avocado, red onion, salt, black pepper, olive oil, lime juice, chicken breast, blackened seasoning, frozen cilantro lime rice) are each used by a step. No step uses anything not on the list.

prose.intro_html:
Blackened chicken with mango salsa is proof that eating like you are on vacation and eating like you have a budget are not enemies. You get a fast, peppery sear on chicken breast, a bright mango and avocado salsa that does the heavy lifting on flavor, and a bed of cilantro lime rice underneath to make it a real meal. No fussy technique, no ingredient you have to hunt down at three stores.

Here is the part I like. One serving lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, and the carbs come from an honest bowl of rice, not from a sauce doing math tricks. That is a dinner that feeds you, keeps you full, and does not wreck the grocery bill. We are scaling it to 14 containers, so you cook once and eat all week.
prose.shop_smart:
This one is friendly to shop for because almost everything is whole produce and one freezer item. Here is how I fill the cart for 14 servings:

  • Mangoes and avocados: you want about 3 1/2 large mangoes and 3 1/2 large avocados. Buy them a touch firm a few days out and let them ripen on the counter so they are ready on prep day, not mush.
  • Cilantro: plan on about 3 1/2 bunches (roughly 7 oz once chopped). Fresh, not dried, this is the whole personality of the salsa.
  • Red onion and limes: a couple of medium red onions covers the 1 3/4 you need, and 2 limes gets you the 3 1/2 tablespoons of juice for the salsa.
  • Chicken breast: 5 1/4 lb of boneless skinless breast. Buy the big family pack and dice it yourself at home instead of paying for pre-cut.
  • Frozen cilantro lime rice: grab seven 10 oz bags. The freezer aisle version cooks in minutes and keeps this a weeknight job.
  • Blackened seasoning and oil: 6 tablespoons of blackened seasoning and 7 tablespoons of olive or avocado oil, which we divide between the salsa and the searing.
prose.make_it:
1. Make the mango salsa. Dice the mangoes and avocados, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion. Add them all to a large bowl. Hit it with a pinch of salt and pepper, pour in a tablespoon of the oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until everything is coated and combined. Taste it and adjust the salt.

2. Season the chicken. Dice the chicken breast into 1 inch cubes. Add the blackened seasoning and toss until every piece is well coated.

3. Sear the chicken. Heat the rest of the oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high. When it is hot, add the chicken in batches so you do not crowd the pan. Cook about 3 minutes per side, until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches an internal temperature of 165 F. Let it rest while you finish the rice.

4. Make the cilantro lime rice. Cook the frozen cilantro lime rice bags according to the package directions. That is the whole job here.

5. Build the bowls. Lay down a bed of rice, top with the blackened chicken, and spoon the mango salsa over the top. Divide across your containers and you are done.
prose.portion_html:
Do not eyeball this. Cook everything, then portion by weight so all 14 containers come out even. Add up the cooked rice, the rested chicken, and the salsa, weigh the total, and divide by 14. That number is your per-container weight. Scoop rice first, then chicken, then a spoon of salsa on top, and check each one against the scale as you go. Even portions mean every serving actually hits {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein, not just the first three off the top.

Keep the salsa portioned right on top and these hold well in the fridge through the week.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is what makes this a keeper. Real chicken breast, real produce, and a bright salsa, and it still comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is the whole point of cooking once and portioning fourteen ways: you buy the family pack, you use every bit of it, and the price per dinner drops through the floor. Compare that to what a single takeout bowl with the same ingredients would run you.

head.description: Blackened chicken with fresh mango avocado salsa over cilantro lime rice. A budget high-protein meal prep dinner scaled to 14 servings, 43 g protein each.

steps: Dice the mangoes and avocados, chop the cilantro, and mince the red onion into a large bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper, add a tablespoon of the oil and the fresh lime juice, and toss until well combined.
Dice the chicken breast into 1 inch cubes, add the blackened seasoning, and toss until every piece is evenly coated.
Heat the remaining oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high. Sear the chicken in batches about 3 minutes per side until it reaches 165 F internal, then let it rest.
Cook the frozen cilantro lime rice according to the package directions.
Build each bowl with a bed of rice, the blackened chicken, and a spoon of mango salsa, then divide evenly across all 14 containers by weight.
